thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — PR #3897 is ready for security/privacy review. It touches the on-prem auth proxy and adds a new VPC egress rule for telemetry ingestion. Hoping for a quick sign-off before tomorrow's merge window (10:00am PT).

chris: Link? I can take a look now. Is this the change that swaps token projection to use service-account-proxy?

maya: Yep — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3897 :point_right: Summary in the PR body.

sarah: Pinging to grab context. Quick skim: I saw an env var rename + a new config block under deploy/onprem/telemetry.yaml. Can you paste the config snippet here?

chris: Snippet from the PR:```yaml
telemetry:
  enabled: true
  egress:
    cidr: "10.200.0.0/16"
    allowed_destinations:
      - telemetry.internal.redwood:443
auth_proxy:
  token_source: "service-account-proxy"
  sa_audience: "redwood-infer/onprem"
```

maya: Also added a small migration job that rewrites a couple of config keys for existing clusters. It's in the deployment change set.

sarah: Quick notes from security review:
- Do not commit any long-lived credentials — I found one placeholder in migration job using `ROUTER_ADMIN_KEY` — please ensure it's read from KMS at runtime. :no_entry_sign:
- Confirm KMS policy: which key will be used and who can decrypt? We need key ACLs for the onprem cluster's node pool.
- VPC egress CIDR looks fine but add explicit Egress allowlist for telemetry.internal.redwood only (no 0.0.0.0/0).

maya: Good catches — the ROUTER_ADMIN_KEY is a leftover, I'll remove and update to call KMS client. For the KMS key, we plan to use `projects/redwood/keys/onprem-telemetry` (I'll add the policy link).

alex: @sarah quick question: will the token projection flow require any additional RBAC on the control plane? I want to know if we need a short maintenance window.

sarah: Yes — the SA used by the proxy needs permission to impersonate the router-sa. That's a 2-minute rollout change (bind/unbind). We should schedule during the merge window but can do it in the same slot.

ops-oncall: Ops note: if we change the policy, have a rollback plan ready. Recommend a short canary to one cluster, validate telemetry and auth flows, then expand.

chris: Proposed plan: merge during 10:00–11:00am PT slot, immediately run the migration job in canary, validate logs + token exchange. Rollback steps in PR description (revert deploy + run reverse migration).

maya: ok I'll: 1) remove hardcoded key 2) add KMS policy link 3) add canary checklist and smoke commands 4) ping infra to hold a 30-min rollback window.

sarah: Thanks — after you push the fixes I can run a quick sandbox test and give final :thumbsup:. If anything looks off I'll call for a forced hold.

maya: Pushed fixes — removed leftover, added KMS key doc and smoke test commands. @sarah @alex can you re-review when you have a sec? :pray:

sec-bot: Automated secret-scan: no high-severity findings in latest diff. (scan id: scan-2026-03-17-88) :mag: :white_check_mark:

sarah: Re-reviewed — LGTM on security side assuming infra confirms the KMS ACLs. :eyes: I'll approve once infra confirms.

ops-oncall: Infra confirmed KMS ACLs will be updated as part of the rollout. We can proceed with the 10:00am PT merge window.

alex: Approved from my side. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks all — merging at 10:00am PT and running canary on cluster `onprem-canary-3`. I'll post results here.

chris: Thanks — I'll stand by for smoke results and help revert if needed.

maya: (post-merge) Canary passed basic auth + telemetry checks. No regressions observed in 15m. Expanding to rest of clusters now. :tada:
